title: Journalist & Whistleblower Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Essential privacy and security checklist for journalists and whistleblowers to protect sources, communications, and sensitive information.
intro: Journalists and whistleblowers face unique privacy challenges when handling sensitive information and protecting sources. This comprehensive checklist covers essential security measures to safeguard communications, maintain anonymity, and protect against surveillance.

items.why: Signal provides end-to-end encryption and disappearing messages to protect source communications from interception.
items.howTo: Download Signal, enable disappearing messages for all conversations, and verify safety numbers with contacts. Always use Signal over regular SMS or email for sensitive communications.

items.task: Set up ProtonMail or Tutanota for secure email
items.why: Encrypted email services protect sensitive correspondence and prevent unauthorized access to your communications.
items.howTo: Create accounts with ProtonMail or Tutanota using a pseudonym. Enable two-factor authentication and use only over Tor for maximum anonymity.

items.task: Use Signal or Jami for voice calls
items.why: Encrypted voice calls prevent eavesdropping on sensitive conversations with sources or colleagues.
items.howTo: Install Signal or Jami for voice calls. Always verify you're using the encrypted calling feature, not regular phone service.

items.task: Use dedicated devices for sensitive work
items.why: Separate devices prevent cross-contamination of personal and professional communications and reduce tracking risks.
items.howTo: Purchase phones with cash, use prepaid service, and avoid linking to personal accounts. Replace devices regularly and dispose of them securely.

items.task: Use Tor Browser for sensitive research
items.why: Tor Browser routes traffic through multiple servers to hide your IP address and browsing activity from surveillance.
items.howTo: Download Tor Browser from the official website. Always use it for researching sensitive topics or accessing sources. Never log into personal accounts while using Tor.

items.why: VPNs encrypt your internet connection and hide your real IP address from ISPs and potential surveillance.
items.howTo: Choose services like Mullvad or IVPN that don't keep logs. Pay with cryptocurrency if possible. Use VPN in combination with Tor for maximum protection.

items.task: Use Incognito Browser for privacy-focused browsing
items.why: Incognito Browser provides built-in privacy features and blocks tracking without requiring complex configuration.
items.howTo: Download Incognito Browser for daily browsing activities. It automatically blocks trackers and ads while providing a clean browsing experience for research.

items.why: Private search engines don't track your searches or build profiles about your research interests.
items.howTo: Use DuckDuckGo, Startpage, or Searx instead of Google. Set one as your default search engine in all browsers.

items.task: Enable full disk encryption on all devices
items.why: Disk encryption protects all data on your device if it's lost, stolen, or seized by authorities.
items.howTo: Enable FileVault on Mac or BitLocker on Windows. For Linux, use LUKS encryption. Always use strong passwords for encryption keys.

items.task: Create encrypted backups of important data
items.why: Encrypted backups ensure you don't lose critical information while maintaining security if devices are compromised.
items.howTo: Use VeraCrypt to create encrypted backup drives. Store backups in secure locations separate from your main devices. Test restore procedures regularly.

items.why: Normal deletion doesn't actually remove files from storage, leaving sensitive data recoverable by adversaries.
items.howTo: Use BleachBit on Linux, Eraser on Windows, or built-in secure empty trash on Mac. Regularly wipe free space to remove deleted file traces.

items.task: Remove metadata from documents and images
items.why: Metadata can reveal location, device information, and editing history that could compromise your identity or sources.
items.howTo: Use tools like ExifTool or MAT2 to strip metadata before sharing files. Check document properties and remove personal information before publishing.

items.why: Face-to-face meetings may be necessary but require careful planning to avoid surveillance and protect source identity.
items.howTo: Meet in public spaces with multiple exits, leave phones at home, vary meeting locations, and use counter-surveillance techniques. Consider using coded language.

items.why: Physical and digital documents from sources need special handling to prevent tracing back to the original source.
items.howTo: Use SecureDrop if available, or encrypted USB drives passed through intermediaries. Scan and digitize physical documents, then securely destroy originals.

items.why: Consistent security practices prevent patterns that could expose your sources or compromise ongoing investigations.
items.howTo: Vary your routines, use different routes and locations, avoid discussing work in unsecured locations, and train colleagues on security protocols.

items.why: Knowledge of shield laws and legal risks helps you better protect sources and prepare for potential legal challenges.
items.howTo: Consult with media lawyers, understand local shield laws, document your newsgathering process, and prepare for potential subpoenas or searches.
